cohort: 1,183 obese pregnant women and 5,399 normal or underweight pregnant women at the Department of Obstetrics of a differentiated perinatal care facility in Portugal
finding: Obesity during pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of cesarean section, gestational diabetes, hypertensive pregnancy disorders, and large-for-gestational age infants, but not preterm birth, fetal/neonatal deaths, low birthweight, or neonatal ICU admissions.
mod_finding: Obese pregnant women were significantly more likely to have cesarean sections.
